Parent: #245.

**Current-source update after #252 (2026-09-26):** The prerequisite generic file-save cutover is in `main` through PR #253. Current production uses `SaveFile` opcode 20 with one frozen final `Base`/`Local`/`Zero` stream; `EditFile`, `ConstructFile`, the old Begin descriptor route, direct Workspace range entrypoints and the FUSE ioctl callback have been removed. The source diagrams and code links below describe their historical pinned revisions. For new work on this issue, preserve the current generic route and prove larger-run scaling, amortized cursor traversal, bounded resources, writer progress across Commit phases and incremental-head correctness. The owner accepted 1,024 separated runs for #252 and directed no further 4,097 rerun in that sub-issue; #248's independent larger-scale gate remains open.

**Public API benchmark requirement (owner direction, 2026-09-26):** The 4,097-separated-final-run timed gate must enter through public `WorkspaceApi::mount` → `WorkspaceApi::exec` → `WorkspaceApi::commit`. The Exec command runs ordinary file syscalls against the mounted Workspace path (for example, one shell-launched program performing 4,097 positional writes); the measured driver must not call `Workspace::own_payload`, `Workspace::write_file`, FUSE callbacks, Bridge, service, or C1 directly to create the changes. Those internal calls made by the product behind the public API remain part of the measured work. Record Exec, Commit, and cleanup wall separately, plus the complete-command budget and cache contract. The retained #252 4,097 diagnostics and 1,024 pass used native existing-file handles, with no mounted/FUSE writes; they are useful diagnostics, not this public API benchmark. Internal count-driven probes may diagnose the cost but must be labeled separately from the API gate. Current source imposes a 30,000 ms whole-Exec deadline (`WORKSPACE_EXEC_MAX_MS`) and kills the shell process group when it expires. Owner direction (2026-09-26) is to remove this product runtime ceiling; #249 owns the control-protocol, daemon, and SDK change. Record Exec wall, and keep the 60 s functional harness ceiling and the repository performance budget as measurement gates; neither is a product command-kill timer. Do not change the 4,097-write workload to make a row fit. A normal performance-selection admission also needs its own repository budget and cache-qualified receipt.

**Namespace-cardinality sibling:** [#256](https://github.com/Ephemeral-AI-Lab/layerfs/issues/256) removes the separate 128 dirty-identity/changed-name and 32 KiB prepared-metadata ceilings for many-tiny-file package updates. This issue's 4,097 final runs belong to one dirty file, so passing #248 does not satisfy #256; both are required for #245's package-scale claim.

## Execution plan on the current `SaveFile` source (2026-09-26)

The historical design and source links below predate #252. Its streaming `SaveFile` route, separate stream-byte budget and removal of the 4,096 payload-record admission cap are already on `main`; verify the current source before implementing any older step.

1. **Freeze the public workload and evidence contract.** Prepare one closed existing-file master, then use an independent writable copy per run. The measured driver uses only public `WorkspaceApi::mount`, one `WorkspaceApi::exec` that launches one writer process issuing exactly 4,097 separated positional file writes through the mount, and `WorkspaceApi::commit`. Record the actual FUSE-write count, final changed-run count, Exec, Commit, complete command and cleanup. Verify exact new bytes and the old head independently through public access. Record Exec wall and retain the 60 s functional harness ceiling; the whole-Exec product timeout is removed under #249. A performance selection has the repository's separate complete-command limit of 15 s by default, or a 25 s exception declared before its one sample; its cache state must be controlled and recorded. A timed-out or cache-ineligible row remains nonpassing.
2. **Diagnose the public path early, without using a performance rerun.** Reuse #252's native receipts as diagnostics. Run one labeled, count-driven API diagnostic at a smaller fixed write count with checkpoints, plus a same-range overwrite control if needed. Count FUSE callbacks, payload records examined by routine cleanup, page-file creates/allocations, ownership-ledger reads/writes, extent-tree page visits, root publications, and time by acquisition/publication. Use external tracing or legitimate production telemetry, not a benchmark driver that calls internal mutation methods or test-only product hooks. Do not pre-run the predictably over-budget 4,097 case on unchanged source.
3. **Make accepted writes scale.** Replace routine full-record cleanup polling with work-triggered reclaim candidates while preserving quota-pressure/scoped cleanup, ownership, unknown-outcome custody and bounded memory. Then reduce whichever per-write backing operations the API diagnostic shows dominate. Start with existing-format measures such as safe handle reuse or coalescing ownership work within one atomic publication; change to packed page storage only if the measured budget still requires it. Keep read-your-writes and one atomic local-root publication per accepted mutation. Target path-local `O(log P)` extent work and no scan of all earlier writes' retained records.
4. **Finish Commit scaling on the existing route.** Keep `SaveFile` and its bounded service spool. Make ordered extent/descriptor/replacement walks monotone with amortized `O(H+P)` page visits per pass, and release the Workspace mutation gate during `O(P)`, `O(R)` and `O(S)` Commit work. Count C1 mapping visits and deferred bytes at increasing final-run counts. Replace per-run split/concat only if those counts or the API Commit gate show it is necessary, while preserving the exact canonical root and mapping partition for previously accepted inputs.
5. **Prove correctness, then run the gate once at a frozen source identity.** Cover 249/250-leaf transitions, a focused >65,535-run sequence, overwrite/adjacent/no-op/zero/deletion cases, malformed input, two incremental heads and a write accepted during each relevant Commit phase. After focused checks pass and the source, driver, fixture, cache contract and budget are sealed, take one 4,097-run public API attempt per source/arm. That same receipt records Exec and complete functional wall against the harness budgets and, only if cache-qualified, the registered performance gate; keep failures and cleanup evidence. Run the independent verifier once at matching identities. A smaller matched API baseline may be registered before implementation for a speed comparison; native timings are never its control. Diagnose any miss from the receipt and count-driven evidence, change source, then evaluate that new source identity without resampling an unchanged arm.

**Sequence:** implement this follow-up only after package E and the package F candidate arm. The [E/F final report](https://github.com/Ephemeral-AI-Lab/layerfs/blob/d6bc594f2/core/docs/issues/245/evidence/phase1-e-f-final/REPORT.md) records both complete at `ff3dbcfe0`; start from the accepted post-E/F source and keep their receipts unchanged. This is a separate file-delta scope, not a rerun of F or a claim that its cache-ineligible latency cells passed.

## Why

Package D removed the 256-descriptor Begin-frame and 8 MiB replay ceilings, but one existing file still hits a **4,096 final changed-run ceiling** during Workspace writes/lowering, Bridge validation, or C1 construction. The limit is an implementation budget for materialized descriptors, not a property of a file or a requirement to checkpoint each write. It conflicts with [#245's target](https://github.com/Ephemeral-AI-Lab/layerfs/blob/d6bc594f2/core/docs/issues/245/ARCHITECTURE.md#bounds-speed-target-and-limits-of-the-claim) to avoid a fixed changed-interval count.

The Workspace already keeps a live, path-copied `Base` / `Local` / `Zero` **final extent sequence** so accepted writes are readable. Commit derives aggregate changed runs from one frozen version; it does not need the history of shell calls:

```text
base:          a b c d e f g h
shell writes:    b->X, b->Y, c->Z, g->Q   (4 WRITE calls)
final file:    a Y Z d e f Q h
final delta:    [b,c -> Y,Z] [g -> Q]      (2 changed runs)
```

Today the aggregate still becomes several count-sized allocations and C1 applies each *final run* through private split/concat work:

```text
live final extent tree
  +-- write-time Fold.edits / inode u16 count ------> 4,096 refusal
  +-- Commit lower_file -> Vec<Edit> -> packed Vec -> 4,096 refusal
                       -> Bridge Begin(count) + body -> 4,096 refusal
                       -> server block + edits + starts Vecs
                       -> C1 EditStream Vec -> compare/build -> 4,096 refusal
```

Removing one check or raising the number merely moves the failure. The server and C1 must still validate and replay the final delta without retaining an array proportional to its run count.

## Proposed algorithm: aggregate once per frozen file version

1. **Keep live range COW, not canonical write checkpoints.** Continue path-local `Base` / `Local` / `Zero` updates and their atomic local-root publication for read-your-writes. Do not persist a list of prior WRITE calls or publish a canonical Store file version after each. Remove the edit-run count as a write admission rule and resolve the `u16` inode count / `u16::MAX` sentinel without replacing 4,096 with a larger fixed count. Keep the existing file-length, private-backing, page, and deadline protections.
2. **Freeze and summarize the final state at Commit.** Package E's capture pins G1 while new writes enter G2. An ordered, bounded cursor over G1's extents maintains only `base_cursor`, result-coordinate delta, pending non-Base length, descriptor count, replacement-byte total, and checked length totals. At each next `Base(offset, length)`, close one maximal run replacing `base_cursor..offset` with the pending `Local/Zero` bytes; advance the base cursor. Close a nonempty/deletion tail at EOF. This is the final aggregate, independent of overwritten intermediate values and shell-call count. Validate monotone base ranges, exact coverage, replacement totals, and final length.
3. **Replay the immutable aggregate rather than materializing it.** The current generic `SaveFile` metadata declares extent count and byte totals before the body. First pass computes/validates them; a second cursor emits packed 24-byte descriptors into fixed-size frames; the existing replacement source emits only final `Local/Zero` bytes. Keep the cursors monotone across frame pulls so frames do not repeatedly seek the same tree paths. Cross-check emitted count and totals against pass one. The `u32` declared count may remain for framing with checked arithmetic; it is not a 4,096-run admission rule. All passes belong to Commit's work, including any timed Commit phase.
4. **Validate and replay at the service.** Parse descriptors incrementally with bounded RAM, validate ordering/current-result coordinates/overlap/length and exact EndInput totals, and retain a quota-charged replayable descriptor stream plus the existing bounded replacement spool. C1 can replay both for its comparison and construction passes without descriptor/offset `Vec`s.
5. **Build one final canonical result.** C1 consumes ordered retained base spans and final replacement runs, reuses untouched canonical subtrees by identity, and holds only a bounded tree/CDC frontier. It may do work for each *final* run, but must not publish an intermediate file checkpoint/root per run or retain drafts proportional to the number of past writes. Seal only nodes whose boundaries cannot change, then emit one final file root and preserve one Branch-head publication. Preserve current edit-boundary CDC and exact-root semantics for previously accepted inputs; if a bulk builder would change roots, obtain an explicit versioned identity ruling before shipping it.

```text
shell/POSIX writes --> live final range tree --> freeze G1 --> G2 accepts writes
                                               |
                          pass 1: count + validate final delta
                          pass 2: stream descriptors (fixed buffer)
                          pass 3: stream final Local/Zero bytes
                                               |
                         Bridge frames -> service replay spool
                                               |
                         C1 compare -> final mapping -> one file root
                                               |
                                      one Commit publication
```

## Incremental Commit invariant

For a linear sequence in one Workspace, each successful Commit installs the **immediately preceding Commit's file roots and filesystem root as the next base**. `expected_head` pins that predecessor; a moved external Branch head is a conflict/rebase decision, never permission to diff against a stale ancestor. "Compare against Commit n" means using its authenticated base roots and checking only changed ranges, not reading every byte of Commit n.

```text
C_n:       file root R_n, filesystem root F_n
  |
  +-- G_(n+1): local final extents over R_n
  |       Commit (n+1): aggregate delta(G_(n+1), R_n)
  |                     expected_head = C_n; base = F_n
  |                     --> C_(n+1), file root R_(n+1)
  |
  +-- G_(n+2): writes accepted after G_(n+1) was frozen
          temporary base = captured G_(n+1) file version
          after C_(n+1) succeeds, substitute R_(n+1) as that base
          Commit (n+2): aggregate delta(G_(n+2), R_(n+1))
                        expected_head = C_(n+1)
```

For example, if C_n contains `abcdef`, G_(n+1) changes `b` to `X`, and a later generation changes `e` to `Y`, C_(n+1) is `aXcdef` and the next Commit describes only `e -> Y` against that saved version. It does not resend `b -> X` or replay both generations. Unchanged files retain their prior content IDs. Advance the live base only after a known successful outcome; preserve the frozen root and explicit failure/unknown-outcome custody.

## Concurrency boundary

The mounted filesystem can receive operations from multiple processes, and accepted writes after G1 capture belong to G2. Their local publication is atomic; the new delta path must preserve that behavior. **The present public control route admits only one live session (Q=0): two independent `WorkspaceApi::exec` calls, or an `exec` and a `commit` control call, are not concurrently admitted by that daemon.** This issue does not claim otherwise or widen control-session admission. A single shell command may spawn concurrent processes that access the same mount; direct mounted activity can also overlap a Commit once a control call is available. Keep Commit/Stage serialized by the Workspace's one retained submission slot, while FUSE writes proceed in the successor generation. Independent concurrent SDK `exec` calls require their own control-lane work and proof.

Let `P` be extents in the frozen final sequence, `R` its final changed runs, `S` actual replacement bytes, and `H` bounded tree height. The count/descriptor walks visit `O(P)` extents each; instrument page visits so repeated frame pulls do not multiply that traversal by `H`. Wire and temporary spool space cost `O(24R + S)` **actual input bytes**. Resident memory should depend on `H`, page/CDC windows, and fixed I/O buffers, **not `R` or the number of earlier WRITE calls**. Dense final fragmentation necessarily costs at least `Ω(R)` descriptor/output work; target construction proportional to visited mapping nodes, `R`, and changed bytes, without repeated whole-base work. A sparse delta should reuse untouched base payload and mapping subtrees. Keep a declared stream-byte/disk budget and precise `Capacity`/deadline failure; do not disguise a count ceiling inside `input_length <= MAX_FILE` (which currently includes descriptor bytes).

## Acceptance

- A file with **4,097 separated final runs** passes the genuine Workspace → Bridge → service → C1 save path and exact-byte/readback oracle; its previous head remains readable. A focused sequence test also exercises **more than 65,535** runs so the `u16` count does not become the next cap. Do not inflate the existing mounted route's 60 s budget to force a 4,097-WRITE setup to fit; record any unrun mounted cell honestly.
- Many overwrites of the same range and adjacent changes aggregate by final state, not write count. Cover insertion, deletion, truncation, `Zero` holes, no-op base-root reuse, and current-result coordinate arithmetic.
- Two sequential Commits on the same file prove the second `SaveFile` names the first Commit's saved content root as its base and includes only second-generation changed runs. Cover a write accepted during the first Commit's frozen G1 window; verify both heads, the live successor, parent-head checks, and no old delta replay.
- For inputs the old path accepts (≤4,096 runs), require **identical canonical root and mapping partition**, not merely equal bytes. For >4,096 runs, verify final bytes/root deterministically and previous-head readback. Malformed ordering, overlap, truncation, and count/byte mismatch fail before publication; spool cleanup and known/unknown outcome custody remain correct.
- No fixed run-count rejection survives in the write fold, inode record, lowering, Bridge, service, or C1. A real file-size, stream-byte, backing-disk, resident-memory, or deadline exhaustion still fails explicitly and leaves no partial publication.
- Use count-driven diagnostics at increasing `R` (including 4,096 and 4,097) to report descriptor/replacement bytes, extent and mapping-page visits, cursor reseeks, untouched base bytes read, peak resident/draft bytes, and spool high-water. Show bounded memory and no full-base payload read for a sparse edit. Preserve #245's G1→G2→G3 capture/reconciliation proof; do not reuse the F arm as a new performance sample.

**Source anchors:** [Workspace fold and count](https://github.com/Ephemeral-AI-Lab/layerfs/blob/d6bc594f2/core/crates/layerfs-workspace/src/backing/metadata_pieces.rs), [final-delta lowering](https://github.com/Ephemeral-AI-Lab/layerfs/blob/d6bc594f2/core/crates/layerfs-workspace/src/commit/lower.rs), [upload buffer](https://github.com/Ephemeral-AI-Lab/layerfs/blob/d6bc594f2/core/crates/layerfs-workspace/src/commit/upload.rs), [Bridge budget](https://github.com/Ephemeral-AI-Lab/layerfs/blob/d6bc594f2/core/crates/layerfs-bridge/src/contract/request.rs), [server replay](https://github.com/Ephemeral-AI-Lab/layerfs/blob/d6bc594f2/core/crates/layerfs-server/src/service/save/edit_stream.rs), [C1 stream and boundary semantics](https://github.com/Ephemeral-AI-Lab/layerfs/blob/d6bc594f2/core/crates/layerfs-content/src/file/edit/input.rs).

## Source-audited implementation gates — 2026-09-26

The detailed [Commit-time delta algorithm and complexity study](https://github.com/Ephemeral-AI-Lab/layerfs/blob/7939c56d1/core/docs/issues/245/FINAL_DELTA_COMMIT_COMPLEXITY.md) and [private page-tree study](https://github.com/Ephemeral-AI-Lab/layerfs/blob/7939c56d1/core/docs/issues/245/PRIVATE_BACKING_AND_PAGE_TREE.md) are committed at [`7939c56d1`](https://github.com/Ephemeral-AI-Lab/layerfs/commit/7939c56d1) and reviewable in [PR #250](https://github.com/Ephemeral-AI-Lab/layerfs/pull/250). They inspect source `74ac30e28`; strict E and the frozen F comparison completed at product source `b2cd0df23` (F latency remains INELIGIBLE).

Keep the existing #248 acceptance, with these explicit prerequisites:

1. `PayloadHost::reserve` caps **live payload records across the host at 4,096**, independently of edit runs. A 4,097-separated-write end-to-end gate must track this count and admit by actual backing resources, or it can fail before Commit despite removing every descriptor guard.
2. The first 249 leaf pages (30,753–30,876 nonmergeable extent records) appear to reach a singleton-branch packing refusal; at 250 leaves (30,877 records), a narrow height-2 splice may mix child levels that the cursor rejects. These are **source-derived risks, not reproduced failures**. Build deterministic 249/250-leaf boundary and first/middle/last-subtree splice tests, repair any confirmed failure, then claim height-scalable range COW.
3. `metadata_cursor::step_in` rereads ancestors per leaf, and `ReplacementSource::pull` reopens a cursor per pull. Instrument page visits and reseeks. The target is amortized `O(H+L)` page visits per ordered tree pass, not merely bounded cursor heap.
4. `Request::validate` still compares `24R + S` input length with the 4 GiB logical file cap. Separate declared stream-byte/disk admission from logical file length so descriptor overhead cannot become a hidden run ceiling.
5. C1's `EditStream(Vec<Edit>)`, `Plan`, and indexed `EditSource` cannot consume a sequential replay spool without changing the interface. Preserve the current exact canonical root and mapping partition for previously accepted streams. A forward-only builder that changes CDC boundaries needs an explicit versioned identity decision before implementation.

Measure resident memory, file-backed page cache, descriptor/payload spool high-water, C1 draft bytes, mapping visits, untouched base bytes read, and actual quotas as `R` grows. A `>65,535`-run fixture must also prove the `u16` inode count/sentinel is not a replacement ceiling. No performance result is inferred from this research.

## Full-Commit write-progress gate — 2026-09-26

The [source-pinned phase audit](https://github.com/Ephemeral-AI-Lab/layerfs/blob/3b7917e60/core/docs/issues/245/ARCHITECTURE_COMPLEXITY_RESEARCH.md#what-writes-continue-during-commit-currently-proves) corrects an overbroad interpretation of E. E proved one accepted mounted write during a held successor-builder page **read**, not all Commit phases. Today `lower_file` holds the metadata writer gate across its full frozen extent walk and `ReplacementSource::pull` reacquires that gate for each transfer pull. A mounted write using `writer_until` can wait behind either and time out; the bounded, ungated Commit-time cursor/replay path must remove those long mutation-gate holds as well as the 4,096 count-sized allocations.

Add deterministic barriers and count-driven diagnostics for a write during file lowering, descriptor production, replacement transfer, remote C1 construction, and reconciliation. Record writer-gate hold/wait, page/window ownership, accepted revision, deadline outcome and exact saved/live bytes. The target is no mutation gate held for `O(P)`, `O(R)` or `O(S)` Commit work. It still allows brief capture/install ordering points and precise quota, deadline or custody refusal. Independent `WorkspaceApi::exec`/Commit control overlap remains #249's separate daemon requirement.

comments.body:
The current-source file-tree capacity and complexity review for #248 is in draft PR #257: https://github.com/Ephemeral-AI-Lab/layerfs/pull/257

At f74dbe77, 4,097 isolated one-byte final changes need an optimistic 68 packed file-tree pages (272 KiB), while 4,097 distinct private one-byte payloads allocate about 32 MiB before ledgers, reservations and pinned COW versions. The report identifies the 249-leaf branch transition, mixed-level splice, resumable cursor, long Commit writer hold, and shared payload/ledger lookup costs as implementation and proof work. These are source-derived findings, not a measured public API speed result. #256 separately owns changed-file/name cardinality.

## Phase 1 (shared #248/#256 ownership substrate) implemented and measured

Branch `codex/issue245-post-phase1-implementation`, based on `origin/main`
`f74dbe77d` (the current post-#252/#255 source).

- `b298d175d` instrument(core): count routine private-ownership work
- `7e6cac877` perf(core): index the ownership registry and drive reclamation by work

**Public route.** In-process public Workspace API: `WorkspaceHost::new` →
`Workspace::attach` → `Workspace::own_payload` / `Workspace::backing_status` /
`Workspace::reclaim_payloads`, over real Linux ext4 private backing. No private
Workspace/Bridge/C1 mutation call, no test-only product hook, no new product
counter that gates an operation. The counts come from two new saturating fields
on the existing `BackingStatus` observation (`routine_scans`, `lookup_scans`),
on the same footing as the projection counters.

**What the count trace found.** Routine `PayloadHost::maintain` ran before every
accepted mutation and walked the whole ownership registry from its head looking
for one reclaimable record. With `N` retained acquisitions the next write paid
`N` and a run paid `N(N+1)/2`: for 1,024 retained one-byte inputs, 523,776
record examinations, `routine_per_write` 0.0, 4.0, 35.5, 159.5, 383.5, 767.5 at
1, 8, 64, 256, 512, 1,024 accepted writes. Separately, `Arena::payload` served
one frozen-Commit piece with a linear registry search.

**What changed.** The registry is now `BTreeMap<payload-id, Arc<Record>>`
(`O(log N)` by-id lookup, iteration still in id order), a candidate's one
custody page carries its payload id (`Vec<(PageRef, payload-id)>`) so releasing
custody is indexed, and routine reclamation drains a release list filled at the
exact moment a record can become garbage (last external `OwnedPayload`
reference dropping, or its custody page being released) instead of searching.
The deliberate scoped pass walks with an ordered cursor and re-derives the
aggregate flags once per pass. Charged allocation keeps a fixed 32-byte
per-entry registry charge instead of a doubling vector reserve.

**Gate evidence (after).** 1,024 retained inputs: `routine_scans` 0 (was
523,776), `lookup_scans` 0, `allocated_bytes` 1,024 × 8,192 exactly. Releasing 5
of them costs exactly 5 examinations on the next write while 1,019 stay
retained; 256 released owners behind one live reader pin cost exactly 256 and
the pin survives; a 512-input accepted-and-dropped churn holds one record and
one 8 KiB segment at a time and costs 511 examinations in total. The deliberate
scoped pass still reports non-zero `lookup_scans` and releases exactly the
owners it names — the control that the routine count is an absence of walks, not
a dead field.

**Quota/failure custody (unchanged and re-proved).** A full private quota refuses
the next admission with `Backing { phase: Acquire, kind: StorageFull }`, charges
nothing and drops nothing: the existing owner, its 8 KiB allocation and its
segment files stay accounted and readable. The existing owned-payload route
`core/crates/layerfs-workspace/tests/payload_route.py` passes **13/13** checks at
these product inputs (reader pins and admission, exact-block quota reuse,
collider retention, corruption-driven explicit cleanup, native short-write
retention, native ENOSPC retention, local progress and window headroom, clean
close).

**Receipts.** `core/docs/issues/245/evidence/post-phase1-ownership-v1/`:
`before-count-trace.txt` + `receipt.json` (baseline), `after-count-trace.txt` +
`after-receipt.json` (fix, counts and route), `payload-route/` (raw route
result). Product inputs `sha256:cf34a7a5…82fe9e`; release binaries
`sha256:a3f9b000…dab435` and `sha256:0ccdb226…e4eb23`; image
`rust@sha256:e51d0265…c0bc4` on aarch64 Linux 6.12.76 ext4 (4,096-byte blocks).

**Checks and their exact status.** release `cargo test -p layerfs-workspace
--test backing_ownership`: PASS 4/4, 0.47 s. `payload_route.py`: PASS 13/13,
cleanup PASS. `cargo build --release --locked --workspace --all-targets`: PASS.
release Clippy workspace/all-targets: no error and no warning in any changed
file. `cargo fmt --check`: PASS. `check_product_boundary.py`: PASS (295 files).
`core/tools` unit tests: PASS (9).

**Nonpassing / not run.** The mounted FUSE/daemon route, Commit, C1/C5 and the
Linux stage fixture (not prepared in this environment); the wider `#[ignore]`d
route selection; every timed, cache-qualified or performance row — none is
claimed, and no wall number in the receipts is a speedup or admission PASS.

**Production LOC.** `b298d175d`: 124599 → 124642 (+43). `7e6cac877`:
124642 → 124683 (+41). Phase cumulative 124599 → 124683 (+84); core 55871 →
55955, legacy unchanged.

**Next on this issue (phase 2).** File extent and frozen Commit path: height
transitions, monotone cursors, short writer-gate holds, bounded C1 replay, then
the public 4,097-separated-write Exec → Commit gate with exact old/new bytes and
roots. Phase 2 is not started and no part of it is claimed here.

## Phase-2 slice: three structural defects in the extent sequence, fixed with counted evidence

`5a9a9fc5f` on `codex/issue245-post-phase1-implementation` (parent `7e6cac877`).
Focused external tests over the real page codec and the same traversal the
mounted path uses; **no mounted route, Commit or timed row is claimed.**

Three defects, all reachable from an ordinary file operation, found by adding
boundary cases the existing 24 extent-sequence tests never reached:

1. **A legitimate file could not be written at all.** `pack` filled each branch
   greedily (248 children, then the remainder), so 249 leaf pages packed as
   `[248, 1]`; `encode_pieces_branch` refuses a branch with fewer than two
   children, so the splice returned `Capacity`. Every leaf count congruent to
   one modulo the fanout (249, 497, 745, …) was affected. `pack_level` now
   splits each level into its fewest chunks of nearly equal size.
2. **A tall file became unreadable after one narrow write.** `descend` answered
   with its collected children, one level below the node it replaced, so a
   splice into a tree whose root sits at level 2 returned a frontier mixing
   untouched level-1 subtrees with folded level-0 leaves; the rebuild relabelled
   from level 1 and the cursor then refused the published tree (`Io`, "levels
   are relative"). Reproduced at 65,536 separated one-byte extents (529 leaves):
   the splice returned `Ok` and the next walk of that root failed. `descend` now
   returns pages that all declare the replaced node's own level and each branch
   packs its rebuilt children up to that level.
3. **The declared 4 GiB maximum was not representable.** `PieceRecord::parse`
   accepted `offset + length` only to `2^32 - 1` while `MAX_FILE` is exactly
   `2^32`, so the last record of a full 4 GiB base read failed to parse and the
   whole sequence was unreadable. Now bounded by `MAX_FILE`; 4 GiB round-trips
   as 257 records with the last one ending exactly at the file bound.

**Counted evidence** (`tests/pieces_sequence.rs`, 27/27 PASS, 0.16 s): 4,097
separated runs read back exactly, one narrow splice reads 2 and writes 2 pages;
65,536 separated runs make 529 leaf pages, one narrow splice reads 3 and writes
3 pages; 249 leaves pack into branches that all hold ≥ 2 children. Receipt:
`core/docs/issues/245/evidence/post-phase1-extent-v1/receipt.json`. Production
LOC 124683 → 124729 (+46); core 55955 → 56001.

**Still open here, and refused rather than corrupted:** a fold that replaces an
entire sibling subtree with a single page leaves that child one level below its
own, which needs borrow/merge rebalancing across siblings. Such a splice now
returns `Capacity` instead of publishing a non-uniform tree. Narrow writes
anywhere in a tall file are unaffected.

**Nonpassing row — the public gate is NOT RUN.** This issue's phase-2 gate is
4,097 separated writes through public `mount` → one `exec` → `/bin/sh -c` →
`commit` with exact old/new bytes and roots. It needs the Linux mounted harness
(prepared master + `benchmark_shell`/`verify_shell` release binaries + the daemon
image + a privileged FUSE mount) and a prospectively frozen scenario in the
shell registry; that harness is not prepared in this environment, and no attempt
was made, so there is no receipt to report. It is not blocked by the code above:
the 4,097-run shape is a 2-level tree and is exercised directly by the new
focused case. `NOT_RUN` — next actionable step on this issue.

**Phase-2 extent-tree slice: collapsed-node lifting (2026-09-26 implementation lane).**

Commit: `0c3e455bd` on `codex/issue245-post-phase1-implementation` (parent `5a9a9fc5f`), pushed.

Route/API: the private length-indexed extent sequence behind every accepted mounted write (`WorkspaceApi::mount` -> POSIX/FUSE callback -> `metadata_pieces::replace`). No public API, wire format or canonical Store format changes.

What changed: a fold that replaced a whole subtree rebuilt that node one level below its own and was refused with `Capacity`; `lift` now answers one rebuilt inner node at its own declared level (>=2 children pack as before, exactly one is lifted inside a single branch page of its own level, none drops the node). The root is unchanged: it still adopts a single page and loses a level. The pieces branch codec accepts one child (still refuses zero).

Why this shape rather than sibling rebalancing: borrowing from or merging with a sibling restores a two-child shape only when enough pages exist (three pages cannot be spread over two nodes without leaving one with a single child) and it reads and rewrites a sibling this splice would otherwise share. The lifted page replaces the node one for one, so a collapse adds no page and no height, and a repeated collapse over the same range rewrites that one page instead of stacking a level.

New: two-level tree of 249 leaf pages folds its whole first level-1 child (125 leaves, 15,500 bytes) into one lifted page, stays height-uniform, 30,876 bytes read back in order; second fold over the same child keeps 125 leaves and one lifted page; deleting the whole child drops the node and the root loses a level. Each case asserts every branch's children declare exactly one level below their parent, and that the earlier generation still reads what it published.

Separately, `RootOwner::write_raw_page` still refuses a fold that writes more than 128 pages into one candidate root (charged temporary-page growth is the shared page-store item). #248's 4,097 separated-run public gate is not run here and is not claimed.

**Correction to my phase-2 comment above, plus the sweep it was missing.**

I retract one claim I published there: that the 128-page candidate temporary list and the 64-page ledger-table allowance are "still open fixed aggregate refusals that bind well before quota, near ~1 MiB allocated". That came from a misdiagnosis. The 126-write failure I based it on was the boundary-insertion bug (`metadata_pieces.rs`, fixed in `c3fd065c6`), not either ceiling. Measured now on the same public route (`Workspace` attach -> 384 accepted appended writes on one file, distinct payload each):

| writes | cumulative `metadata_reads` | page reads per further 64 writes |
| ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 64 | 2,458 | 38.4 |
| 128 | 8,779 | 98.8 |
| 192 | 11,755 | 46.5 |
| 256 | 18,089 | 99.0 |
| 320 | 21,385 | 51.5 |
| 384 | 27,547 | 96.3 |

Per-write page reads oscillate between roughly 46 and 99 and do not grow with retained acquisitions, so there is no `O(N)` per-write term to report, and no evidence that either ceiling binds at 384 writes. What is true is weaker and source-only: `RootOwner::write_page`/`write_raw_page` (`ownership.rs`) still refuse at 128 temporary pages per publication, `Arena::reserve_ledger_identity` refuses a candidate with a 64-page allowance, and the arena's ledger identity table is clamped at 1,058 entries. No test in this lane covers a publication that writes more than 128 pages or a candidate with a 64-page allowance, so they are **unverified candidates**, not demonstrated refusals. Treating them as open refusals was wrong.

Also added since that comment: `e8a97c8c6` sweeps fourteen extent counts at the leaf and branch boundaries (1, 123-125, 247-250, 496-498, 30,875-30,877), each built, spliced in the middle, appended at the end and read back, checking the level invariant, the root level the fanout requires, and exact in-order coverage. Phase 2's "height-uniform at every count and pack shape" is now swept rather than sampled at a few shapes: `-p layerfs-workspace --test pieces_sequence` PASS 33/33 in 0.17 s.

The one evidence gap I keep: "no Commit phase holds the metadata writer gate across a frozen walk or a transfer pull" is enforced by construction (no `writer()` call remains in `lower_file`, `FileUpload::descriptor_bytes` or `ReplacementSource::pull`) and the route case checks admission between two transfer frames, but a deterministic overlap check needs the seccomp page-read barrier from the recorded E/F fixtures and is not taken.

**Phase-2 closure reopened on three named items (handoff `f98afe38f`).**

My "phase 2 closed" comment overstated the case. The code properties are implemented and covered, but closure rests on:

- **2.R1** a deterministic overlap check for the writer-gate property. It holds by construction (`lower_file`, `FileUpload::descriptor_bytes`, `ReplacementSource::pull` no longer acquire the gate) and `tests/commit_progress.rs` only shows a mounted mutation admitted *between* two transfer frames. The check that would fail if the gate returned needs a page read held inside each frozen phase, using the seccomp `pread64` listener the E/F fixtures already carry in `tests/commit_staged.rs`.

Mounted route: 384, because one accepted write costs roughly 50-100 metadata page reads and the route case would exceed the 30-second test rule. Either the per-write page cost comes down from the count, or the largest shape that fits is recorded with its limit and is not called the 4,097 row.
- **2.R3** one scope decision: `commit/directories.rs` still takes the writer gate around its namespace reads while the phase's sentence says "no Commit phase". Narrow them under #248 or state the sentence covers the file phases its title names and leave them to #256.

Also recorded: a collapsed node is repaired by level-preserving lifting rather than sibling rebalancing, and that property is met and swept at fourteen boundary counts, so rebalancing is not open work.

**Correction: the 4,097 mounted-route item is not phase-2 scope (handoff `a1bc905d5`).**

Owner direction is that the 4,097-separated-run public row is verified in the mini-benchmark lane, so the item I filed here as "2.R2 - the phase's own count through the mounted route" is withdrawn. The implementation obligation is only that the shape is representable, which is already covered at the extent level (`tests/pieces_sequence.rs`, 4,097 separated runs) and through the mounted route at a declared smaller count (`tests/commit_progress.rs`, 384 appended writes).

Phase 2's closure therefore rests on two items: 2.R1, a deterministic overlap check for "no Commit phase holds the metadata writer gate across a frozen walk or a transfer pull", and 2.R2, one scope decision about the writer-gate holds in `commit/directories.rs`. The per-write metadata page-read count (roughly 50-100 per accepted write, `BackingStatus::metadata_reads`) stays recorded as a diagnostic, not as an admission criterion for this phase.

**Phase 2 remainder 2.R1 closed: the writer-gate property now has a deterministic check.**

Commit: `007d53552` on `codex/issue245-post-phase1-implementation` (parent `c30fe68a0`).
Route: the public Workspace API over real Linux backing - `WorkspaceHost::attach` → `mknod`/`open_file`/`own_payload`/`write_file` → `Workspace::commit`. No mount, no daemon image, no prepared Store; the delivery is a fake `OperationDelivery`.

**What was missing.** `tests/commit_progress.rs` showed a mounted mutation admitted *between* two transfer frames. It cannot fail if the gate comes back around a walk - the two syscalls may fall far apart. The claim "no Commit phase holds the metadata writer gate across a frozen walk or a transfer pull" had no check that would fail.

**What the new check does.** `tests/commit_overlap.rs` reuses the recorded E/F page-read barrier: a seccomp `pread64` user-notification listener installed on the Commit thread, so one page read of the frozen transfer stops in the kernel while the test reads the gate state, runs an ordinary mounted mutation through the same handle, and then answers the read with `CONTINUE`.

Gate state is read from `MetadataStatus::working_bytes`: a held writer gate adds exactly `WORKING` (640 KiB) to the pre-Commit baseline, so a charge below `baseline + WORKING` is a read taken with the gate free. The test answers every read the Commit starts on the way to the held one and counts how many reported a held gate, so it asserts on more than the single read it held.

**Measured (locked release, one test binary, `--nocapture`):**

| arm | page held | charge vs baseline 4304 | phase | frames | mutation | outcome |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | ---: | --- | --- |
| frozen walk | `m-page-*` | 69072 (gate **free**) | Preparing | 1 | `write_file` through the same handle | **admitted**, 2.5 ms |
| control (gate-held bookkeeping) | `m-ledger-*` | 659664 = baseline + 640 KiB (gate **held**) | before any frame | 0 | the same `write_file` | refused `Busy`, 1 µs |

`scans_with_gate = 0` across every read the Commit started while the transfer was live. The control arm exists so a barrier that intercepted nothing cannot report every phase as clean.

**Suite wall: 0.09 s** (cap 30 s). The shape is deliberately small (6 extents): the barrier turns every metadata page read on the Commit thread into a kernel round trip, so the property is carried by *which walk owns the read*, not by the extent count.

**2.R2 is out of phase 2 by owner direction** - the 4,097 separated-write route shape belongs to the mini-benchmark phase, so no route case is added here and none is claimed. For the record, the per-write cost was diagnosed before dropping it: **56.5 / 91.6 / 107.6 metadata page reads per accepted write** over three rounds of 64 chosen writes, at 31 / 49 / 59 ms per write, i.e. ~4-8x over the 30 s rule at 4,097 writes. Recorded as the reason; not replaced by a smaller row.

**2.R3 recorded as a scope decision, not a code change.** Phase 2's "no Commit phase" covers the file phases its title names. `commit/directories.rs` keeps its two `host.writer()?` holds around the namespace reads (lines 90, 120); #256's keyed namespace work narrows them.

Checks run: locked release build of the covering test binaries; `commit_overlap` 2 passed; `commit_progress` 1 passed (15.5 s); release `cargo clippy -p layerfs-workspace --all-targets` no error; `cargo fmt --all -- --check` clean; `core/tools/check_product_boundary.py` PASS (295 files); `core/tools` unit tests 9 passed. Production LOC 56142 → 56142 (delta 0), core 56142, legacy 68728, combined 124870 via `core/tools/production_loc.py`; test-only change.

Limits: the check proves the gate is free across a transfer walk it holds, on this fixture's shape; it does not bound how long a walk may take, and it is not a timing or throughput claim. The successor-builder overlap remains covered by the ignored mounted fixture in `commit_staged.rs`.
